The Arab Kings.

the king said to the Arabs who were guarding him,
"Put irons on this man and on those who are with him."
And when they had put them on,
the king sent to those who were in the city that they should surrender the city {OCR?} and live.
And they obeyed him,
and surrendered it to the Arabs.
Now the people of Tyre, although they were about to surrender it,
a certain count whose name was the Marquis (Conrad of Montferrat) came to them,
and he guarded it well.
And from there Saladin went against Jerusalem and encamped against it.
And he set up great mangonels against its wall on the northern side,
because that area was wide and suitable for the encampment of warriors.
And he waged a fierce battle against it for three days.
And again the Franks took courage,
because there were in it sixty thousand fighting men, horsemen and foot-soldiers,
and they went out against the Arabs,
and killed many of them.
And on that day, Izz al-Din Isa, the lord of Qal'at Ja'bar, was killed,
as well as other notable men.
Then the Arabs fought by shooting arrows,
and drove back slightly those who were upon the wall,
until the men of Aleppo reached the wall.
And quickly they dug out stones from it with their craft,
and made breaches,
and propped them up with timbers,
so that when they should set fire to them and they should burn,
the wall would fall.
Now the Franks, when they despaired of help,
sent two prudent men to Saladin,
and requested from him a promise for their lives.
Saladin, however, refused and said,
"I will not conquer it except by the sword,
and I will deal with you just as you dealt with the Arabs who were in it
when you captured it,
for you killed and took captive."
Then one of those two Franks said to Saladin,
"I have another word to say to you,
O Sultan,
if you promise me that you will not become angry."
And the Sultan said,
"There is no anger with me;
speak whatever you wish."
And that Frank said,
"Had we not known your discernment,
and that you cannot violate the ancient custom of kings—
that when their enemies are defeated and lay down their weapons and ask for peace,
they no longer contend with them—
we would not have come out to you.
